guidance.heading: 2026 Financial Outlook
section: (assumes an average foreign exchange rate of US$1=C$1.38)
Telesat is reiterating its 2026 GEO segment guidance provided in March:
● | GEO revenue to be between $300 million and $320 million;
● | GEO Adjusted EBITDA1 to be between $210 million and $230 million, excluding non-recurring debt refinancing costs.
Telesat is adjusting its Telesat Lightspeed spending forecast to reflect the expected timing of satellite and launch payments:

● | Total spending on the Telesat Lightspeed program, including both expensed and capitalized costs, is now expected to be in the $1.1 billion to $1.3 billion range, compared to the $1.3 billion to $1.5 billion range we provided when we reported second quarter 2026 earnings.

Telesat’s quarterly report on Form 6-K for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, has been filed with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Canadian securities regulatory authorities, and may be accessed on the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov and on the System for Electronic Document Analysis and Retrieval+ (SEDAR+) website at www.sedarplus.ca.

desk.headline: Revenue down 20% to C$81m, loss widens; 2026 GEO guidance reaffirmed, Lightspeed spending forecast cut

other.label: Net loss
other.change: vs C$121.1m loss a year ago

results: Revenue fell 20% to C$81m as broadcast contracts ended or shrank and some older satellites were retired.
Adjusted EBITDA fell 74% to C$12m; without C$25m of debt-refinancing costs, it fell 41%.
Net loss widened to C$157m, mainly from a non-cash charge on Lightspeed financing warrants.
In August it signed a C$2.7bn deal (with options) to serve the Canadian Armed Forces in the Arctic, funding growth of Lightspeed to 225 satellites.
Cash rose to C$814m, helped by C$510m of customer prepayments in the first nine months.

guidance.summary: 2026 GEO revenue and adjusted EBITDA ranges were reaffirmed. Lightspeed spending for 2026 was cut to reflect the timing of satellite and launch payments.

points: Global Lightspeed service slipped about three months to around end-Q2 2028; Arctic service still targeted for around end-Q1 2028.
First two satellites to launch around mid-2027, with full launches of 15 satellites each from around September 2027.
Refinancing GEO debt, which starts to mature later this year, is a key priority; management would not speculate on issuing equity.
Management sees more defence and sovereign deals, mostly closing during 2027, but said timing is hard to predict.
GEO revenue is expected to keep falling into 2027.

First Lightspeed launches in mid-2027 and any further schedule slips.
New government and defence contracts added to backlog.
